configuration-not-read-intro: The target's package.json holds configuration this run could not use. Each line below says what this run did with its entry, and every account in this report is the one the target gives without it.
configuration-wrong-kind: {entry} is {is} where {reads} is read, so this run read it as absent.
configuration-unknown-key: {key} is not a key the specController block reads, so this run read nothing from it.
runner-key-not-a-layer: {key} — not a layer: the runner block is keyed by the four layers, and this key excludes nothing.
not-checks-entry-matches-no-step: {key} entry {entry} matches no step of the workflows this run read, so it makes no step a non-check.
not-checks-entry-not-a-step-name: {key} entry {entry} does not name a step as `<workflow file>:<job id>:<step name>`, so it makes no step a non-check.
scenario-code-errors-framing: {count} — each misfiles a scenario code, so the by-feature cut below cannot be trusted, and the run fails (exit 1). Every account still reconciles as it would if the code were filed correctly.
several-scn-codes-framing: {count} — each is a scenario carrying more than one scenario code, so no account was raised for it under any of them, and the run fails (exit 1).
misfiled-and-several-scn-codes-framing: {count} — each either misfiles a scenario code, so the by-feature cut below cannot be trusted, or is a scenario carrying more than one scenario code, so no account was raised for it under any of them. The run fails (exit 1).
duplicate-scn-code-not-listed: A duplicated @SCN code is not listed here: it is reported on its account's rows, as "{outcome}".
duplicate-feature-code: the feature code @{code} is carried by {fileCount} feature files — {files}. A feature code names exactly one feature file: a reconciliation's by-feature cut groups on it, so two files sharing a code report as one row and attribute one file's scenarios to the other. Give one of them a code of its own.
foreign-scn-code-carried: {file} carries the feature code @{featureCode}, but holds the scenario @{scnId}, whose feature part names {named}. A reconciliation's by-feature cut groups on the id, so it counts this scenario under {carrierCount, plural, one {{carriers}'s row, not {file}'s. Re-code the scenario for @{featureCode}, or move it to {carriers}.} other {the one row for {named}, which {carrierCount} feature files carry — {carriers} — so that row cannot say which of them it belongs to. Re-code the scenario for @{featureCode}, or move it once a single file carries {named}.}}
foreign-scn-code-no-carrier: {file} carries the feature code @{featureCode}, but holds the scenario @{scnId}, whose feature part names {named}. A reconciliation's by-feature cut groups on the id, so it opens a row for {named}, which no feature file carries as its header code, so that row stands for no file. Re-code the scenario for @{featureCode}.
no-feature-code: {file} carries no feature code, but its scenarios carry @SCN codes. A feature file is the class its scenarios' codes are filed under: give it a header code of its own, and code its scenarios for it.
several-scn-codes: {file}'s scenario "{scenario}" carries {codeCount} @SCN codes — {codes}. A scenario is one account, so it raises its evidence obligations under none of them, and a test citing any of them cites a code no scenario carries. Give it one code.
run-unsound: **This run is unsound.** {proofs} A broken proof sits on the row of the claim it names, as every Evidence Observation does. On a scenario's row, an Evidence Obligation of its kind of quality check that no other proof answers reads "Evidence Observation is missing", though its test may already be written. A broken proof on the row of a phantom claim or of the unnamed claim may be the proof behind any item of its kind of quality check that reads "Evidence Observation is missing", on any row. Fix what stopped each proof listed below from running, such as its test, the code it loads, its step definitions, its runner or the CI job that runs it. Then run them again and regenerate this report.
scenario-code-errors-gloss: the corpus files a scenario code under the wrong feature, so the by-feature grouping cannot be trusted. Read `{heading}` above.{alsoOutOfBalance} This run FAILED.
several-scn-codes-gloss: a scenario in the corpus carries more than one scenario code, so no account was raised for it under any of them. Read `{heading}` above.{alsoOutOfBalance} This run FAILED.
misfiled-and-several-scn-codes-gloss: the corpus files a scenario code under the wrong feature, so the by-feature grouping cannot be trusted, and a scenario in it carries more than one scenario code, so no account was raised for it under any of them. Read `{heading}` above.{alsoOutOfBalance} This run FAILED.
also-out-of-balance: The accounts do not agree either: at least one Claim Reconciliation carries a reconciling item.
out-of-balance-gloss: the accounts do not agree. At least one Claim Reconciliation carries a reconciling item. This run FAILED.
unsound-gloss: the evidence could not be TRUSTED to reconcile. A proof never ran, so the behaviour it proves was never exercised. Read the run-integrity stamp above before any count below it.
pending-gloss: every Claim Reconciliation balances, but Pending Items are outstanding and this run treats a deferral as a failure (`--strict`). This run FAILED.
balanced-gloss: every Claim Reconciliation balances: every Evidence Observation satisfies its Evidence Obligation.
nothing-to-reconcile-gloss: there were no accounts to agree. The ledger carries no Claim Reconciliation at all, so this run has NO BASIS FOR A VERDICT — the corpus `{corpusDir}` carried no scenario and nothing was produced. Not balanced: a run that examined nothing must not certify.
pending-items-outstanding: Pending Items are outstanding — deferred, not out-of-balance, so the verdict stands. A run that treats a deferral as a failure gives exit 3 under `--strict`.
